back2basics.text: Non-tariff barriers are trade restrictions that do not involve tariffs but can include quotas, import licensing, sanitary regulations, and other measures that restrict imports or exports. They can limit market access and affect trade balances by making it harder for foreign goods to compete. Understanding these barriers is essential for analyzing international trade relations and negotiations.

back2basics.concept: Emergency and Governor's Rule in Federal Systems
back2basics.text: Emergency provisions allow a central government to assume control over a state or province in cases of law and order breakdown or security threats. Governor's rule is a form of direct federal administration where the governor exercises executive powers, often replacing the elected government temporarily. These measures are usually constitutionally regulated and require legislative approval to ensure checks and balances.

body.label: Scheme overview
body.text: PM-AJAY is a centrally funded scheme by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment aimed at socio-economic and educational empowerment of Scheduled Caste communities.

body.label: Three components
body.text: The scheme includes development of Scheduled Caste-dominated villages into Adarsh Grams, Grants-in-Aid for socio-economic projects at State and District levels, and construction and repair of hostels.

body.label: Adarsh Gram concept
body.text: An Adarsh Gram is a model village where basic services are accessible, minimum needs of all sections are met, and disparities are minimized, focusing on Scheduled Caste-majority villages.

sections.heading: What is the PM-AJAY scheme and its objectives?

body.label: Village coverage
body.text: Over 47,200 villages benefiting more than 47.79 lakh citizens have been covered, with 18,093 villages declared Adarsh Grams as of September 8, 2026.

body.label: Development works and plans
body.text: A total of 46,944 development works have been completed and 27,032 Village Development Plans prepared under the scheme.

body.label: Hostel infrastructure
body.text: 785 student hostels have been completed, with Rs 61.46 crore allocated for FY 2026-27 to build two hostels accommodating 264 students.

sections.heading: What progress has PM-AJAY made so far?

body.label: Funding details
body.text: Approximately Rs 1,730 crore was released as Grants-in-Aid directly to States and Districts from FY 2021-22 to FY 2025-26, supporting livelihood and skill development projects.

body.label: Fund utilization
body.text: Up to 50% of funds may be used for gap-filling in selected Adarsh Gram villages; 5% for Technical Support Groups and Project Implementation Units; 2% for hostel construction and repair.

body.label: Monitoring mechanisms
body.text: The PM-AJAY Mobile App and Portal enable real-time digital processing, improving transparency, accountability, and efficiency in scheme implementation.

sections.heading: How is PM-AJAY funded and monitored?

body.label: Empowerment focus
body.text: The scheme addresses multiple empowerment dimensions including infrastructure, livelihoods, skill development, and education for Scheduled Castes.

body.label: Reducing disparities
body.text: By developing Adarsh Grams and improving socio-economic indicators, PM-AJAY aims to reduce disparities in Scheduled Caste-majority villages.

body.label: Supporting education
body.text: Hostel construction under the scheme facilitates access to quality education for Scheduled Caste students from rural and remote areas.

back2basics.text: Electoral roll revision is the process of updating the list of eligible voters to ensure accuracy and inclusiveness. back2basics.concept: El Nino and its impact on Indian monsoon
back2basics.text: El Nino is a climate phenomenon characterized by the warming of sea surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean, which affects global weather patterns. In India, El Nino often leads to weaker monsoon rains, causing droughts and water shortages. This impacts agriculture, water availability, and power generation, especially hydroelectricity, making it a critical factor in planning for climate resilience and energy security.

2026-10-17-am-bf837d7bf6.deck: The Telangana government is taking measures to prevent power shortages due to El Nino conditions, including purchasing electricity from other states and promoting renewable energy. This is important for UPSC aspirants to understand the climate-related challenges affecting agriculture and energy security in India.

back2basics.text: Gross Domestic Product (GDP) measures the total value of goods and services produced in a country and is a key indicator of economic health. Growth projections help policymakers and analysts understand the expected pace of economic expansion. Factors like private consumption, investment, exports, and sectoral performance influence GDP growth. External factors such as global trade conditions and domestic factors like monsoon impact agricultural output and overall economic activity.

2026-10-17-am-e5d423d9f7.deck: The World Bank upgraded India's GDP growth projection for FY27 to 7.1% from 6.6% in April, citing better-than-expected economic performance despite global uncertainties. This update highlights key growth drivers such as exports, private consumption, and industrial activity, which are crucial for understanding India's economic outlook.

body.label: Growth drivers
body.text: The World Bank attributed the upgrade to better-than-expected first quarter GDP growth of 7.8%, strong exports, solid private consumption, and robust industrial activity.

body.label: Exports impact
body.text: Exports have outperformed expectations and are seen as the main upside factor for the FY27 growth outlook compared to earlier forecasts.

body.label: Consumption trends
body.text: Rural consumption initially led growth supported by agricultural performance and income support, while urban consumption strengthened later due to tax relief and GST cuts.

body.label: Industrial performance
body.text: Industrial activity exceeded expectations with infrastructure and construction goods growth accelerating to 7.2% in Q1 and electricity sector expanding by 9.3%.

sections.heading: What are the reasons behind the World Bank's upgraded GDP forecast for India?

body.label: Global uncertainties
body.text: Despite trade tensions and geopolitical uncertainties, India's growth held up better than expected, although global uncertainty weighs on private investment.

body.label: Agricultural challenges
body.text: A rainfall deficit during the southwest monsoon weakened agricultural prospects, which could modestly affect rural demand.

body.label: Policy support
body.text: Supportive financial and policy conditions, including stronger public investment, help offset some global risks and sustain growth momentum.

sections.heading: How do external and domestic factors influence India's growth outlook?

body.label: Services sector
body.text: The services sector growth remains elevated despite a slowdown from a high base in FY26.

body.label: Industry sector
body.text: Industry is forecasted to perform better than initially expected, driven by infrastructure, construction, and electricity sectors.

body.label: Agriculture sector
body.text: Agricultural growth is expected to be weaker due to monsoon rainfall shortages.
